html:
The Guwa, or Koa, were an Aboriginal Australian people of central west Queensland, in the upper Diamantina River country around what is now the town of Winton. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Little is recorded of them. Their land is open grassland and stony downs, part of the Channel Country that drains toward Lake Eyre. Sheep and cattle stations came in the 1870s. Banjo Paterson wrote Waltzing Matilda at a station near Winton in 1895. Neighbours on the map include the Wunumara, the Maiawali and the Yanda. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
